tellings.quote: My interest in the topic resulted from a UFO radar-tracking incident that I had inadvertently witnessed at Malmstrom AFB, Montana, in 1967, involving mysterious aerial objects maneuvering near missile sites outside of the base.

My father, USAF Senior Master Sergeant Robert E. Hastings, was stationed at Malmstrom AFB, Montana in 1966–67 and worked in the SAGE (Semi-Automatic Ground Environment) building which housed the base's sophisticated, NORAD-integrated radar facility.

However, when I mentioned that I had worked as a teen-aged janitor at RAPCON in 1966–67 and had once been told by one of the controllers that Air Force jet interceptors had been scrambled to intercept five UFOs, he interrupted me and said,

plain: As a teenager working as a janitor at Malmstrom, a nuclear missile base in Montana, Robert Hastings says a man in the radar room once called him over to see what they were tracking. On the scope were five "unknowns", the formal term for unidentified objects: "I saw five blips in the sort of northeast quadrant of his radar scope." Hastings, who later wrote the book UFOs and Nukes about UFOs at nuclear weapons sites, tells this first-hand and dates it to 1967; in 2011 he wrote that his father worked in the base's radar building in 1966 and 1967, and in 2024 that the incident, involving "mysterious aerial objects maneuvering near missile sites", is what drew him to the subject. Michels retells it several times, sometimes calling the man an FAA supervisor and sometimes a radar operator, as the start of a story that would mean unknown craft were watching American nuclear weapons.
